stories.headline: State Department weighs sharing passport records to verify voter citizenship
stories.summary: The State Department is assessing how to let state and local officials — and some nonprofits — check federal passport records to confirm registered voters are U.S. citizens ahead of the November midterms. A department spokesperson said the goal is sharing that protects Americans’ data, deters fraud, and supports citizenship integrity; DOJ disclosed the plan in a court filing last week. The Privacy Act notice could land in the Federal Register as early as Oct. 22, days after the Supreme Court allowed DHS to share citizenship data for voter checks.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo assembly yield stuck near 60% — early stock may stay tight
stories.summary: A supply-chain source told China’s Jiemian News that Foxconn’s final-assembly yields for Apple’s first foldable were only slightly above 60% as of Sept. 17, and that mature yields could take another six months to a year under current quality bars. Samsung Display foldable OLED panels and hinge parts have also seen low yields and redesigns; Apple’s 2026 global stocking target is pegged around six to eight million units. Pre-orders still open Oct. 16 for the Oct. 23 launch starting at $1,999.

stories.headline: LEGO October 2026 buying guide: PlayStation, Executor GWPs, and Insiders early access
stories.summary: Jay’s Brick Blog’s Sept. 29 shopping guide walks every major Oct. 1 drop — PlayStation 72306, UCS Executor, Downton Abbey, Wallace & Gromit, Holiday House, Pokémon Trainer Moments, and the Avengers: Doomsday wave — plus Gift-with-Purchase windows. Astro Bot 40899 is expected with qualifying Oct. 1 carts, and Executor buyers from Oct. 1–10 get Darth Vader’s Lightsaber 40897 while stocks last. Insiders early access still unlocks several big sets on the 1st before general release.

stories.headline: Penguins open Wednesday at Flyers in a Keystone playoff rematch
stories.summary: Nearly five months after Philadelphia beat Pittsburgh in a six-game first-round series, the rivals open the 2026-27 season Wednesday for the first time since 2021. Crosby said last year’s playoff run raised expectations and the challenge is to elevate again; Arturs Silovs is expected to start with Sergei Murashov as backup. Coach Dan Muse said Bryan Rust’s absence after a strong camp is unfortunate but day-to-day, with nothing set in stone in net.

stories.headline: Jets catch a break: Caleb Williams likely out for Week 4 at Chicago
stories.summary: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bears QB Caleb Williams is on a typical three-to-four-week timeline for a Grade 2 hamstring strain suffered in Week 2, making him unlikely to face the Jets at Soldier Field. That would leave Tyson Bagent (if clear of concussion protocol) or Case Keenum under center for Chicago. New York is 1-2 after losses to Green Bay and Detroit and still sorting its own Hall and Parham injuries heading into the NFC North gauntlet.

stories.headline: Trump denies offering to sell U.S. arms to China’s Xi
stories.summary: President Trump on Monday denied asking Xi Jinping whether China wanted to buy American weapons, contradicting U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue’s Sunday Fox News claim that Trump made the extraordinary offer. “I’ve never heard of that one, I’m going to have to ask him,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Perdue’s comments. The denial lands days after the White House hosted Xi for a high-profile Washington visit.

stories.headline: Meta’s Muse AI agent is coming to smart glasses — ‘Hey Muse’ for on-device tasks
stories.summary: Meta says its Muse AI agent — already topping iPhone App Store charts after a U.S. phone and web launch — will arrive on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses in the coming weeks or months. Wearers can say “Hey Muse” to book appointments, check flights, log meals, or buy products they see while the agent works in a cloud Linux VM and pings back when done. Payments use Stripe Link single-use cards; Meta says Muse data isn’t used for ads, with an optional Confidential VM later this year.

stories.headline: Apple ships macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1 — first bug-fix drop for the new Mac OS
stories.summary: Apple released macOS 27.0.1 on Monday, the first maintenance update to Golden Gate since the mid-September launch, available via System Settings → Software Update. Official notes only say it “fixes unspecified bugs”; companion security updates also shipped for macOS 26.7.1 and 15.8.1. Enterprise docs have pointed to a Platform SSO lock-screen credential glitch among the fixes, while public release notes stay sparse.

stories.headline: Clemson ecologist: delayed Blue Ridge color could mean a more vibrant fall
stories.summary: Warm September weather has kept much of the Southeast green later than usual, but Clemson University ecologist Don Hagan says forests that still hold full canopies could put on a richer red-orange-yellow show if storms stay mild. Peak color usually rolls from Blue Ridge high country into foothills from late September through early November. The Blue Ridge Parkway Association tips mid-to-late October drives that change elevation — Caesars Head, Jocassee Gorges, and long Parkway stretches — to catch sections near peak.

stories.headline: UK family courts: ‘alienating behaviour’ is a fact to prove — not a syndrome
stories.summary: A September 2026 England-and-Wales guide walks how courts now treat parental alienation after Family Justice Council guidance and the landmark Re Y ruling. Judges reject ‘parental alienation syndrome’ as unscientific, require domestic-abuse allegations to be tried before assessing alienating behaviour, and will only instruct HCPC-registered or BPS-chartered psychologists. Transfer of residence remains a welfare decision, not an automatic sanction when alienating behaviour is found.
